literal: To others harm forenoon if one does, to oneself harm afternoon of themselves will come.
translation: If one does harm to others in the morning, harm will come to them of its own accord in the afternoon.
modern: ஒருவர் மற்றவர்களுக்குக் காலையில் துன்பம் செய்தால், அவருக்கான துன்பம் மாலையில் தானாகவே வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet warns about the swift and inevitable return of harmful actions. If a person inflicts pain on others in the early part of the day, pain will naturally seek them out later in the same day. The contrasting words for forenoon and afternoon emphasize that the consequences of evil actions return very quickly, without waiting for another lifetime. The word 'tāmē' (of themselves) shows that this retribution is an automatic, inescapable law of nature.
